_readme: Dependencies referenced by workflow.csv files that are NOT implemented ON PURPOSE, with the reason. The validator (tools/validate_workflows.py) reports them as a WARNING instead of an ERROR, to be able to distinguish 'reference broken by a typo' from 'piece we know is missing and why'. If they're ever implemented, they should be removed from here.

your-handle/gworkspace.reason: It's an INCOMING webhook (Google Workspace Admin SDK, user_created event), not an outgoing REST client. It requires registering an event subscription, exposing a publicly verifiable endpoint, and validating signed notifications. This is a different pattern from every other module in the repo ('handler.py calls an external API'), and depends on hosting infrastructure that RailCall provides, not the module.
your-handle/gworkspace.blocker: Needs RailCall to first define how it exposes webhook endpoints to modules.

your-handle/billing.reason: It's not ONE API: the workflow describes it as 'billing for each provider (OpenAI, Cal.com, Slack)'. Each provider has its own usage/billing API, with different auth, format, and semantics. A single generic 'billing' module would be a made-up abstraction that doesn't correspond to any real service.
your-handle/billing.blocker: Would need to be split into a module per provider (openai-usage, calcom-billing, etc.) or budget-guardian would need to be scoped to a single specific provider.
